timingProxies.scope: Filesystem marker times only: proxies around sequence, not exact worker or active-request boundaries. Per-worker UTC/load not captured and intentionally null.

postRunHost.scope: POST-RUN ONLY; not per-worker host load and not proof of timing isolation

measurementLimits: Node24.22.1, heap1GiB, Linux x64; each worker is fresh, one accepted request/concurrency1. TS loader, fixture construction, imports and Redis seeding precede app wall/CPU interval.
Whole-process current RSS/VmHWM includes preceding allocations; nothing subtracted. Redis-server memory not measured.

Redis CPU is INFO cpu user+sys delta across request interval plus INFO boundary overhead, idle/server background work and scheduling differences; not isolated per-command CPU or a server efficiency claim.
Redis commandstats includes commands executed inside Lua; GET total unchanged. wireRequests field excludes setup/INFO/QUIT and includes the single actual CAS where a consumer saves.
Injected2/10ms timers precede each awaited GET, record batch, index query and fake authorization phase. They model extra latency, not actual measured WAN RTT; CAS is real and un-delayed.
Authorization decisions fake and read-only. No live providers/search/Slack. No request IDs, so no receipt writes during measured workload.
Single pair per workload/condition: no statistical p95 for accepted requests, no discarded samples, no universal speed or CPU/RSS guarantee.

All source-array hashes, bytes, normalized full saved-state/reply hashes and writes match per before/after pair. Only generated mp-/wr- UUIDs normalized in saved/reply hashes; source hashes untouched.
Local after-source is the authorized transport/consumer commits only; helper budgets/UX changes on parent branch are outside this controlled source pair.
